Two passes over all 41 units. `t` was not touched (checked by comparing every `t` before and after). Notes stay within 25–110 words and contain no backticks. gloss.json was not read, as instructed.

Severity: HIGH = wrong sense or wrong claim in a reader-facing field; MEDIUM = misleading or against the house table; LOW = loose wording or small inaccuracy.

## Hand scan of line 91 (flagged AMBIGUOUS, hiatus at Ἄτη)

πρέσ-βα Δι-|ὸς θυ-γά-|τηρ Ἄ-‖ (scansion by the scanner: foot 3 τηρ Ἄ, foot 4 τη ἣ, foot 5 πάν-τας ἀ, foot 6 ᾶ-ται). 15 syllables, six feet. ὸς is long by position before θ (ς + θ). The two scansions differ only in the quantity of the α of Ἄτη/πάντας/ἀᾶται, all within Homeric licence, so the ambiguity is not a fault. What is real is the hiatus: η of Ἄτη cannot elide and stands before ἣ at a comma; it must be kept long. The scanner excuses it as "digamma follows"; I do not accept that for the relative ἥ, so I call it an irregularity of the transmitted line (a hiatus at a pause, not a corruption) and put one sentence in the note.

## The drafter's doubtful points

- δολοφροσύνῃς (97): the form is the dative singular with an unusual ending; sense instrumental ("by trickery"). Rendering "trickery" agrees with δολοφροσύνην (112). Note sharpened (see above).
- Εἰλειθυίας (119): accusative plural, object of σχέθε, with Ἀλκμήνης τόκον as the first object; parallel to μογοστόκοι Εἰλείθυιαι (11.270, checked in the source). `l` "the Eileithyiae" and the 11.270 reference are right.
- ἠλιτόμηνον (118): the note's hedge (formation debated, sense fixed by ἕβδομος μείς) is honest and sufficient; "born before his time" in `i`, "one who had missed his months" in `l` kept.
- ὑββάλλειν (80): "break in" with the "sense not certain" hedge kept; ὑβ- explained correctly now.
- 14.319–320 (note at 122): checked in the source: Δανάης … ἣ τέκε Περσῆα. Correct.
- 14.300: checked: line 14.300 is the same line as 19.106; iliad-088 and iliad-089 give the same English as ours. Correct.
- ὅ = ὅτι at 144: right; a relative would need ἅ to agree with the plural μενοεικέα. Note correct.
- Other cross-references checked in the source and published parts: 7.384 (στὰς ἐν μέσσοισιν), 9.571 (ἠεροφοῖτις Ἐρινύς), 8.398 (ἀγγελέουσαν), 11.270, 1.591 (ῥῖψε), 9.116 and 9.120 (ἀασάμην; line 138 = 9.120), 1.2 (οὐλομένην); 9.505 in the table. All true. Line cross-references inside the part (76, 82, 89, 91, 95, 97, 103, 104, 123) checked against the lines.

## Remembered English

Nothing found that matches a modern translation's wording. The phrases most at risk ("the joy of battle", "mist-walking", "dawdle", "august Ate") are house table entries, the drafter's own rebuilds, or flagged in new-renderings.md.

## Findings considered and refused

- Ἄτη as "Bewilderment" (table row 9.505–512 renders personified ἄτη so): refused. At 9.505 the Greek is a lower-case common noun personified; at 91, 126, 129 and 136 the edition prints the capitalised name of the goddess and calls her Zeus’s daughter, and the note ties her to ἄτη "bewilderment" in its first words. The drafter's choice (and the common noun at 88 as "bewilderment") is defensible and avoids reopening the glosser's concurrent work. The owner may wish to decide this; noted here for LOG.
- 133 ὑπ’ Εὐρυσθῆος ἀέθλων "under the labours" against iliad-049 "from the labours": refused. Different verbs and sense (saving someone from, having work under); the validator rule is for whole units.
- μογοστόκος "travail-bringing" (ambiguous in English): refused; it is the table's rendering (11.270, 16.187) and is used unchanged.
- ἰφθίμην "stock epithet of a wife": refused; table has ἰφθίμη ἄλοχος (5.415).
- 108 `i` ending with a colon while `l` ends with a comma: refused; the oath's content follows in the next unit and the colon is the clearer English.
- "ἐϋστεφάνῳ … as of Mycene, probably the walls as a crown": left as written; the Odyssey table gives ἐυστέφανος of Mycene, and the note hedges.
- 90 θεός "a god": accepted, note says it may be "god" in general.
- The remaining units were checked word by word on both passes and left as they were.

## Pass 2 (gloss)

Scope: gloss.json (68 new forms, 10 broadened). Every parse checked against its line(s) and `l`; 14 keys changed. Broadened entries checked against the glossary as it stood before this part (rebuilt from drafts 001–122): all ten keep the old entry whole. No new key redefines an existing one; every word of the part has an entry; no entry is 230 characters or more; no ASCII apostrophes.

### Wrong (changed)
- `__broaden__` ἔειπον: "aor. 3 sg./3 pl. (same form)" is wrong; ἔειπον is 1 sg. or 3 pl. only (3 sg. is ἔειπε). Now "aor. 3 pl.".
- ἐπιθήσεις: ’you will put an end to (the word)’ misreads τέλος ἐπιθήσεις (`l`: "put fulfilment on the word"). Now ’you will put on’ (with τέλος, ’bring to fulfilment’).
- `__broaden__` θήβῃ: new reading said "Thebes"/’in Thebes’, against the part’s `l`, note and new-renderings.md ("Thebe"; plural Θῆβαι is "Thebes"). Now "Thebe (Boeotian Thebes) … ’in Thebe’". Old text untouched.

### Imprecise (changed)
- εἰλειθυίας: "Ionic -ας" removed; Attic acc. pl. is the same -ας, so it named no difference.
- νεικείεσκον: -ον is also 1 sg.; now "impf. 1 sg./3 pl. iterative".
- `__broaden__` αἵματος: quoted phrase was out of order; now αἵματος ἐξ ἐμεῦ ’of blood from me’.
- ὁρῷτο: Attic equivalent named (= Attic ὁρῴη).
- οὐλομένη: parse reordered (aor. part. mid. fem. nom. sg., then form and Attic ὀλομένη, then use).
- ῥέξαιμι: ’could I do’ (question order) to ’I could do’.

### Line-pinned wording (changed)
- πέσῃ: mother’s-feet gloss shortened to ’be born’; σθενέλου: "husband of the woman whom Hera aids" to "father of Eurystheus" (same as σθενέλοιο); πολλῷ: masc./neut. dat. sg.; ἐϋστεφάνῳ: dat. sg., fem. only where it agrees with Θήβῃ (two-ending adjective, -ῳ is also masc./neut.), "Thebe"; ἐπειγόμενός: ’eager’ (dropped "for war").

### Checked and left
- ἀᾶται (mid. form, active force), ἄσατο, ἀάσθην, ἀνάξει/ἀνάξειν (future of ἀνάσσω), τέξεσθαι (fut. inf.), ἑσταότος, μείς, ἕδρης (Ionic -ης vs Attic -ας after ρ), ἠλιτόμηνον (hedged), λελαθέσθ’, παρασχέμεν, κράατα, βλάβεται, other broadened additions (ἀκούσαι, τῇ, χαλεπὸν, σὸν, κέν, τί, Ἄργος): parse, case and sense agree with the lines.
- Open for the owner: ἄσατο could be the aorist of ἄω ’satiate’ (homograph); not joined, because the form is not so used in this part and nothing in the glossary names it.
